h1: The 6 Best Wi-Fi Smart Plugs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Wi-Fi Smart Plugs 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 Wi-Fi smart plugs scored on platform support, load rating, size and app control, from a Matter mini plug to 4-packs.
summary: The Tapo Matter Smart Plug Mini is the best Wi-Fi plug: Matter certified, 15A and 1800W rated, and compatible with Apple Home, Alexa and Google Home. The Kasa HS103P4 is the easiest 4-pack with a physical button. If you want to stack plugs on a crowded power strip, the Kasa EP10P4 Ultra Mini is slimmer. EIGHTREE and GHome are the budget picks.
intro: Most smart plug regrets come from one oversight: the plug connects to Wi-Fi just fine, but the platform it works with is not the one you use. A plug that speaks only to Alexa and Google will leave an iPhone household with its own app and no Home integration. The wireless chip is cheap; the ecosystem is the real purchase.

We ranked six Wi-Fi plugs by platform support, load rating, body size and control options, scoring each on the Primea framework from its published specs. We also noted when a plug works over 2.4GHz Wi-Fi only, because that single detail decides whether setup succeeds on a modern dual-band router. Prices run from under $25 to the $25 to $50 bracket.

products.name: Tapo Matter Smart Plug Mini
products.verdict: Matter certified, 15A / 1800W and compatible with Apple Home, Alexa and Google Home.
products.description:
The Tapo Mini is certified to the Matter standard, which means it can join Apple Home, Alexa and Google Home without a vendor-specific bridge. It carries a 15A / 1800W maximum rating, a compact body, and LAN control that keeps basic commands local.

It wins because it works with every major platform, where the Kasa plugs list only Alexa and Google. If you ever switch phones or add a HomePod, the plug moves with you. The cost is that you buy it as a single plug, while the others come in 4-packs.

Buy it for mixed or Apple households. At under $25 it is among the cheaper options per unit. Check your router supports the Thread or Wi-Fi setup path the app expects.
products.skipIf: You need four plugs in one order.

products.name: Kasa Smart Plug HS103P4
products.verdict: Four plugs with a touch actuator, no hub required and Alexa and Google support.
products.description:
Kasa's HS103P4 ships four plugs that need no hub, with Alexa and Google Assistant voice control and remote app control. A touch actuator on the body lets you switch the plug by hand when your phone is not nearby.

It ranks second because it lacks Matter and Apple Home support, the two things that lift the Tapo. It beats the cheaper packs on brand support and a polished app, and a physical button is a feature that Govee, EIGHTREE and GHome do not list.

Buy it for an Alexa or Google household that wants four plugs at once. It costs $25 to $50. The caveat is that bulky plugs can block the second outlet on a duplex wall socket.
products.idealFor: Alexa or Google homes wanting four plugs and a manual button.

products.name: Kasa Smart Plug Ultra Mini EP10P4
products.verdict: A 15A ultra mini body that leaves the second outlet usable, in a 4-pack.
products.description:
The EP10P4 is Kasa's ultra mini, rated at 15A, working over 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and with Alexa and Google Assistant. It ships as a 4-pack and costs $25 to $50.

It ranks third because it drops the HS103P4's physical button, and the compact shell means you control it by app or voice only. What you gain is size: on a wall outlet with two sockets, an ultra mini leaves the second socket free, which a bulkier plug will not.

Choose it for dual outlets and tight spaces behind furniture. The 2.4GHz-only listing is the caveat: if your router merges 2.4 and 5 GHz under one name, setup can fail until you split the bands.
products.idealFor: Wall outlets with two sockets and tight gaps.
products.skipIf: You want a manual button or Apple Home.

products.name: Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack
products.verdict: WiFi plus Bluetooth connection, a group controller and custom schedules.
products.description:
Govee's four plugs connect over WiFi or Bluetooth, support Alexa and Google voice, and add a group controller with custom schedules. Costing $25 to $50, they match the Kasa packs on price.

They rank fourth because the listing offers fewer assurances: no stated amperage rating and no manual button. The group controller is the real draw. If you want to switch every holiday light in the house with a single toggle, grouping plugs inside the app is quicker than building a scene.

Buy it if you already use Govee lights and want one app. The Bluetooth fallback is a useful extra when Wi-Fi drops, though range is short.
products.idealFor: Govee users who want grouped control.
products.skipIf: You need Apple Home or a stated 15A rating.

products.name: EIGHTREE 15A Smart Plug 4 Pack
products.verdict: A 15A four-pack under $25 that runs on the Smart Life app.
products.description:
EIGHTREE sells four 15A plugs for under $25, controlled through the Smart Life app, with Bluetooth auto detect and Alexa and Google Home support.

It ranks fifth because it uses a third-party app that is less polished than Kasa's, and it has no Matter or Apple Home. It beats the GHome on amperage, since 15A is stated, and on pack size, since the GHome listing shows one unit. The Smart Life app also works with a large catalog of other devices, which helps if you own cheap smart gear.

Buy it for the lowest cost per plug. The caveat is that apps from budget brands change more often, so expect occasional interface shifts.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who need many plugs.
products.skipIf: You want a polished app or Apple support.

products.name: GHome Smart Plug
products.verdict: A basic Bluetooth or WiFi plug with timers and quick connection.
products.description:
GHome's plug connects over Bluetooth or WiFi, works with Alexa and Google Assistant, and offers app control from anywhere plus outlet timers, all for under $25.

Bottom spot follows from a listing that states no amperage, no pack size and no Matter support, so there is little to verify. Where it fits is the lowest-risk purchase: one plug for a lamp or fan, with the Bluetooth path helping first-time setup.

Buy it to try smart plugs before committing to a pack. The caveat is the missing rating: do not use it for a space heater or other high-draw appliance without confirming the load on the product page.
products.skipIf: You plan to run a high-draw appliance.

whatMatters.detail: Matter is a cross-brand standard that lets one plug work with Apple Home, Alexa and Google Home. Without it, a plug may be tied to a brand app. Check the listing for Matter and Apple Home if you own an iPhone, and avoid assuming Alexa and Google support covers Apple.

Amperage and wattage tell you how much a plug can switch. A 15A / 1800W rating covers most lamps and fans and some heaters. Look for the rating printed on the listing, and avoid using an unrated plug with high-draw appliances. Check the appliance label too, since heaters can pull close to the limit.

Many plugs connect only on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. If your router merges bands, setup can fail. The Kasa EP10P4 states 2.4GHz. Check the listing for the band, and know how to split bands on your router before you begin. Most routers let you name each band separately in their settings.

A bulky plug can cover the second socket of a wall outlet. Ultra mini bodies, like the Kasa EP10P4's, leave space. Check the listing for a mini label and the dimension, especially if you plan to use both outlets. Photos with a hand for scale tell you more than the dimension line.

A physical button lets anyone switch the plug without an app, while groups turn several plugs on at once. The Kasa HS103P4 has a touch actuator and the Govee has a group controller. Check which matters more for your household.

faq.q: Do these work with Apple HomeKit?
faq.a: Only the Tapo Matter Smart Plug Mini lists Apple Home support. The Kasa, Govee, EIGHTREE and GHome plugs list Alexa and Google only, so iPhone households should choose the Tapo.

faq.q: What mistake do people make with smart plugs?
faq.a: Plugging in a high-draw appliance without checking the rating. The Tapo and EIGHTREE list a 15A rating, but the GHome lists none. Confirm the load before running a heater.

faq.q: Is the Tapo worth it over the Kasa 4-pack?
faq.a: For Apple users or anyone who wants Matter, yes. The Kasa HS103P4 gives four plugs and a physical button for $25 to $50, but without Matter or Apple Home support.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Plug it in, open the app, and connect it to your 2.4GHz network. The Kasa EP10P4 is 2.4GHz only, so split your router bands first if setup fails, and keep the phone close to the plug during pairing.

faq.q: What if my Wi-Fi goes down?
faq.a: The Govee and GHome plugs offer a Bluetooth path, and the Tapo keeps LAN control. Kasa plugs have a button on the HS103P4, so you can always switch by hand.

faq.q: Can I use two plugs on one outlet?
faq.a: Only if they are slim. The Kasa EP10P4 and Tapo Mini are compact enough to try, while bulky plugs usually block the second socket. Check the product photos for width.

finalTake: The Tapo Matter Smart Plug Mini is the plug to buy if you want a device that works with every major platform and will survive a change of phone. Choose the Kasa HS103P4 if you want four plugs and a physical button, and the Kasa EP10P4 for tight outlets. The EIGHTREE is the budget answer. Check the load rating before plugging anything hot into any of them.
